artifacts.hook: I trained an AI to spot missing helmets. The hardest part wasn’t the model.
artifacts.caption:
I trained an AI to spot missing helmets. The hardest part wasn’t the model.

Final year projects are often treated as academic requirements. But smart candidates leverage projects to demonstrate skills and passion. It’s crucial to choose a project you’ll be proud to discuss in interviews. 

I spent months building a helmet detection system using YOLOv8. Picking a project based on genuine interest, not just credit requirements, made all the difference. The initial goal wasn’t [your mAP score] accuracy; it was understanding the challenges of real-world data – variations in lighting, helmet designs, and obstructions.

Showing off this project effectively on LinkedIn can significantly boost your profile. Think about it: Recruiters are looking for evidence of your problem-solving abilities and technical skills. A well-crafted project description that highlights your process and results speaks volumes. 

Don’t just list features; tell a story. What problem did you solve? What were the key learnings? 

What’s one aspect of your final year project that you’re particularly proud of? Share in the comments!

Let’s hear about your project!”} 

 🚀 💡
